plans.note: Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) is the operative clause; check mutuality of the cap, whether it is tied to fees paid, and confirm carve-outs (IP indemnity in Section 8, confidentiality in Section 10, willful misconduct) sit outside the cap.

Section 8 should carry Commerce One's third-party IP infringement indemnity in our favour as licensee/host; verify defence/settlement control, remedies for enjoined Software, and that any Corio-side indemnity is narrow and not uncapped.

Grant of Rights plus the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY definitions are the likely vehicles for restrictions on the markets we may serve or competing applications we may host; check Section 13 (Shared Resources) and misc for residual restraints.

Look for any obligation to source hosted procurement software only from Commerce One or to route customers exclusively through it, in Grant of Rights, the revenue-sharing terms and Exhibit D (Sales and Marketing Cooperation).

Pricing (Exhibit B), fees and revenue sharing are where an MFN would sit; confirm any best-pricing or best-terms undertaking runs to us as licensee and that we owe no reciprocal MFN on our customer pricing.

No dedicated non-solicit heading; most likely absent, but scan Miscellaneous, Shared Resources and the support/training provisions (where personnel interact) for an embedded hiring restriction before concluding.

Section 11 (Term and Termination) governs; check whether we have a convenience right on notice without penalty, whether Commerce One has a reciprocal walk-away, and whether termination triggers accelerated fees under Section 4/Exhibit B payment terms.
Auto-renewal mechanics and the non-renewal notice window should be in Section 11; cross-check Exhibit B pricing for uplift on renewal terms.
Governing law, venue and any dispute/arbitration mechanism will be in Miscellaneous; confirm an accepted jurisdiction (likely California here) and courts rather than offshore arbitration.

Assignment clause in Miscellaneous; ensure we may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger without consent, and that our change of control is not a Commerce One termination trigger under Section 11.

Check the DEVELOPMENTS and DOCUMENTATION definitions and Grant of Rights for any sweep of our modifications, configurations or Customer data to Commerce One; Section 6 (Trademarks) and Section 12 (escrow) are related touchpoints.

Section 2/Grant of Rights plus SOFTWARE, CUSTOMER(S), SOFTWARE USER and TERRITORY definitions: confirm the licence extends to our affiliates, contractors and hosted Customers, covers Demonstration Software, and is not revocable at will.

Revenue-share reporting under Section 4 and Exhibit B payment terms is the likely home for Commerce One audit rights over our records; press for notice, annual frequency, business hours, confidentiality and Vendor-borne cost absent material discrepancy.

Screen fees, payment terms and termination for interest, penalties or shortfall/true-up payments imposed on us; confirm any service-level consequences run in our favour rather than as damages against us.

Section 7 (Warranties and Disclaimer) with the Warranty Period and Acceptance Test definitions; assess duration, remedy adequacy and the breadth of the disclaimer, and read against Exhibit C support obligations.

No insurance heading in the outline; likely absent. Confirm nothing is buried in Miscellaneous or the indemnity section before proposing standard coverages given Commerce One's access to hosted environments and data.
Exhibit B pricing, the IMPLEMENTATION FEE and revenue-sharing/minimum guarantees are the likely source of take-or-pay or minimum user/seat commitments on us; check for an exit or reduction mechanism.

Section 11 effects-of-termination should be checked for wind-down/migration assistance and return of our and our Customers' data; Section 12 source code escrow partially serves continuity but is not a substitute for transition help.
